why.quote: If a student takes more than one course from any distribution group, the additional courses can count as upper div electives (with the exception of lower division Philosophy options).
why.reasoning: Turns the catalog's free-text placeholder ('Complete at least 3 of: ...') into a real rule, matching the department's 'Complete at least three electives found on the comprehensive CogSci course list' (same page). The catalog's 249-course list is kept, with two changes. PHILOS W12A, the only lower-division course on it, is dropped because the quote excludes lower-division Philosophy options. The upper-division distribution courses added above (CogSci C102/Psych C129, Psych 122, CogSci C133/Ling C189, Psych 107) are added because extra distribution courses count as electives. Graduate courses on the catalog list (e.g. COMPSCI 287) are kept because they are on the comprehensive list.

why.quote: Complete at least 26 upper division units in the major
why.reasoning: The catalog rules have no unit total. Six distribution courses and three electives are usually around 36 units, but several Philosophy options are lower division, and some electives carry fewer units, so the 26-unit minimum can bind.
